Greek has 'you led... as sheep by Moses and Aaron being led'—God leads, Moses/Aaron lead sheep in simile; [modality] "this at least became known" vs "τοῦτο γνώριμον καὶ ἐμφανὲς ἀνθρώποις ἐγένετο": 'at least' not in Greek; adds concessive nuance absent from source; [completeness] "So the psalm gives this instruction ... in misfortunes" vs "οὕτω δὴ παράγγελμα ὁ ψαλμὸς ... συμφοραῖς διαπρ...": Greek has 'thus then instruction the psalm... in misfortunes...'—translation invents 'gives' and 'this'; source is fragmentary with asterisk; [negation] ""Is the Lord's hand not strong enough to save?"" vs "Μὴ οὐκ ἰσχύει ἡ χεὶρ κυρίου τοῦ σῶσαι;": Greek has double negative 'μὴ οὐκ' = 'Is not the hand... not strong?' i.e. 'Surely the hand of the Lord is strong to save?'—translation flips to single negative question; [scripture] "(Isaiah 59:1-2)" vs "διὰ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου": Citation correct for LXX but should note Hebrew/English numbering if following standard; however LXX Isaiah 59:1-2 matches Hebrew 59:1-2, so this is actually correct; [agency] "which God later declared through Isaiah" vs "ἥνπερ καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα διὰ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου θεὸς ἐξέφηνε": 'later' is interpretive; μετὰ ταῦτα = 'after these things' referring to events, not temporal 'later' in translation's sense; [completeness] "and so on" vs "καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς": Correct translation; no defect | part 2/6: [agency] "as David clearly narrates the events" vs "αὐτοῦ τὰ πράγματα διηγουμένου σαφῶς τοῦ ∆αυίδ": Greek has 'him the things narrating clearly of David' with 'him' (God) as object of standing apart; English makes David narrator, not God.; [modality] "they would have perished and become nameless" vs "ἀπώλοντο ἂν καὶ ἀνώνυμοι κατέστησαν": Greek has 'they would have perished and nameless they would have become' with ἂν only on first verb; English adds 'would have' to second verb not in source.; [completeness] "For God did not approve their choice, but had compassion on their weakness" vs "τὴν μὲν προαίρεσιν οὐκ ἀποδεξαμένου αὐτῶν τοῦ θεοῦ, τὴν δὲ ἀσθένειαν αὐτῶν οἰκτείραντος": Greek is genitive absolute construction, not finite verbs; English supplies 'God' as subject of new sentences, changing syntax significantly.; [completeness] "as in the case of flesh that decays and spirit that departs" vs "ὡς ἐπὶ σαρκῶν φθειρομένων καὶ πνεύματος ἐξιόντος": Greek has 'as upon flesh decaying and spirit departing' with genitive absolute; English adds 'in the case of' and finite relative clauses.; [completeness] "The interpreters have given different accounts of this psalm's subject" vs "∆ιαφόρως τὴν ὑπόθεσιν τοῦδε τοῦ ψαλμοῦ οἱ ἑρμηνεύσαντες ἐκδεδώκασιν": English drops 'differently' (διαφόρως) adverb, making it adjectival 'different accounts' rather than 'differently they have given out'. | part 3/6: [agency] "The interpreters have given different accounts" vs "ὁ μὲν γάρ φησιν... ὁ δὲ... φησὶ... ἄλλοι δὲ": English invents 'interpreters' as subject; Greek uses 'one... another... others' without noun; [modality] "let us set that question aside" vs "ταύτην ἐάσαντες": 'setting aside this one' not 'that question'; no 'question' in source; [completeness] "and examine some of the actual words" vs "τινα τῶν ῥητῶν ἐξετάσωμεν": 'actual words' adds 'actual'; source just says 'some of the statements'; [source_identity] "Ps 78,1b®3" vs "128 Ps 78,1b®3": Missing '128' before psalm citation; this is editorial numbering in source; [modality] "The plea is against the nations" vs "Κατὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἡ ἔντευξις": 'plea' for ἔντευξις is acceptable; but 'is against' adds copula not in source; [agency] "they acted impiously and, being unclean, defiled" vs "δυσσεβήσαντες καὶ ἀκάθαρτοι": English makes 'being unclean' participial circumstance; Greek has two coordinated adjectives/participles as subjects; [negation] "The appeal on behalf of Jerusalem" vs "ὑπὲρ δὲ τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἡ παράκλησις": No 'appeal on behalf of'; παράκλησις is 'exhortation/comfort', not legal appeal matching ἔντευξις; [modality] "once called holy to God" vs "πόλις ἁγία κληθεῖσα θεοῦ": 'once' is added; no temporal marker in source; [completeness] "has become a mound and a heap of stones" vs "χῶμα γέγονε καὶ λίθων σωρὸς": 'mound' for χῶμα is acceptable; but structure is 'a mound it has become and a heap of stones'; [scripture] "Ps 78,1b®3" vs "128 Ps 78,1b®3": Psalm 78 in LXX is Psalm 79 in Hebrew; bracketed Hebrew number missing | part 4/6: [source_identity] "God's servants" vs "δούλους θεοῦ": Correctly translates δούλους, but context shows these are 'slaves' in suffering, not 'servants' in office; [completeness] "which carries a claim of kinship toward God and an appeal to the Master" vs "ὅπερ οἰκείωσιν πρὸς θεὸν καὶ παράκλησιν δύναται πρὸς τὸν δεσπότην": Correct; 'carries a claim' for δύναται is slightly interpretive but acceptable.; [completeness] "there is a sparing of what belongs to him" vs "φειδὼ περὶ τὸ οἰκεῖόν ἐστιν": Correct.; [completeness] "the bodies of the holy ones became food for wild beasts" vs "ὁσίων σώματα θηρίοις γεγενῆσθαι βρώματα": Correct.; [completeness] "their blood was poured out without restraint like water before Jerusalem" vs "τὸ αἷμα αὐτῶν ἀφειδῶς ὕδατος δίκην ἐκκεχῦσθαι πρὸ τῆς Ἱερουσαλήμ": Correct.; [completeness] "Perhaps he calls the fallen "holy ones" because of their original election" vs "ἴσως μέν που καὶ διὰ τὴν ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἐκλογὴν ὁσίους καλῶν τοὺς ἐπταικότας": Correct; 'fallen' for ἐπταικότας ('having-erring/stumbled') is interpretive but acceptable.; [completeness] "just as the apostle also calls holy even the branches broken off for impiety, because they belonged to a holy root (Romans 11:16)" vs "ὥσπερ αὖ καὶ ὁ ἀπόστολος ἁγίας λέγει καὶ τοὺς δι' ἀσέβειαν ἀποκεκλασμένους κλάδους (διότι τῆς ῥίζης ἦσαν ἁγίας)": Correct; note ἁγίας λέγει = 'holy [ones] he-says/calls', with ἁγίας feminine accusative plural agreeing with implied κλάδους understood as branches (masculine) or the construction is slightly irregular; the translation handles this well.; [completeness] "Or perhaps he means that holy ones perished together with the unjust" vs "ἴσως δὲ καὶ συναπολωλότας δηλοῖ τοῖς ἀδίκοις ὁσίους": Correct; 'he means' for δηλοῖ is slightly interpretive but acceptable.; [completeness] "which happens in the capture and destruction of a city and a nation" vs "ὅπερ ἐν ἁλώσει καὶ συντελείᾳ πόλεώς τε καὶ ἔθνους γίνεται": Correct.; [completeness] "and which was shown through Ezekiel as happening. For he says:" vs "καὶ διὰ τοῦ Ἱεζεκιὴλ δεδήλωται γινόμενον· τάδε γὰρ λέγει·": Correct. | part 5/6: [scripture] "Ezekiel 21:3-4" vs "Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ πρὸς σὲ καὶ ἐκπετάσω τὸ ἐγχειρίδιόν μου": Citation should be Ezekiel 21:8-9 LXX (Hebrew 21:3-4); [scripture] "Ezekiel 20:47" vs "Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀνάπτω ἐν σοὶ πῦρ": Citation should be Ezekiel 21:3 LXX (Hebrew 20:47); [agency] "The Lord himself showed that he is the true righteous tree" vs "ὅπερ καὶ τὸ ἀληθὲς δίκαιον ξύλον ἑαυτὸν ὁ κύριος ἐδήλωσε": Greek says 'which thing also the true righteous tree himself the Lord showed'—the antecedent of 'which' (ὅπερ) is the allegorical meaning, not Christ's self-identification as tree; [completeness] "Such was the case of Jeremiah..." vs "—": Jeremiah example belongs to next section, not this source passage

Μὴ οὐκ ἰσχύει ἡ χεὶρ κυρίου τοῦ σῶσαι; is rendered as the rhetorical question 'Is the Lord's hand not strong enough to save?' (Isa 59:1, expecting the answer that it is). Ezekiel 21:3-4 and 20:47 are the English verse numbers of the quoted LXX passages (LXX 21:8-9 and 21:3). The Septuagint sigla (ο') are now rendered. The Jeremiah sentence belongs to this section in the Greek. 'You led the people … as sheep led by Moses and Aaron' reproduces the simile. 'The interpreters', 'set that question aside', 'plea', 'appeal' and 'once called holy' are idiomatic renderings of ὁ μὲν … ὁ δέ … ἄλλοι, ταύτην ἐάσαντες, ἔντευξις, παράκλησις and κληθεῖσα.
